segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making the 10:10 work. I’ve got a hard stop at 10:30 to get the approval packet lined up before noon, but I wanted to handle your seat count and invoice questions live.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sure. We’re at 86 users now, not 80. Finance wants the annual invoice to show 60 seats under operations and 26 under support, same contract, just two cost centers.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. At 86 seats, the annual subscription is $41,280 before tax. Splitting the invoice by cost center is fine, and it doesn’t change the terms or discount.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. We also need the start date to be October 15, but our team won’t really use it until the November 18 go-live. Is that a problem?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No, October 15 works as the contract start. We can schedule onboarding the week of November 4 and keep your go-live target for November 18. The first renewal would be October 15 next year.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s fine. Payment terms are the other thing. Our standard is net 45. Your draft said net 30.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: For a 12-month term, net 45 needs a quick approval, but it’s usually okay at this size. If you’re comfortable with the $41,280 and 86 seats, I can get that cleared and send the updated version this afternoon.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yes, assuming the invoice split is clear. Legal had no redlines except the data processing exhibit, and I think you already accepted that.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, we accepted the exhibit as written. If I’m a little slow replying between one and three, I’m buried in getting the month-end entries cleaned up, but I’ll have your update out by 4:00.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Works for me. Send it to me and copy Nadia in finance. If it matches what we discussed, we can sign tomorrow.
